corrections.what_was_wrong: public/interop/receipts/README.md, published the same morning beside the receipt chain, tells a reader that the chain 'proves these entries existed in this order and have not been edited since the next one was written', and gives a verification snippet. The snippet checks only that each link's prev_hash equals the previous link's state_digest. That check catches a removed or reordered entry, which the page also claims and which is true. It does NOT catch an edited entry: change any field of link N while leaving its state_digest alone and the published snippet still reports zero broken links. The rule that would catch it - how state_digest is computed from a link's own bytes - is not published anywhere on the page.
corrections.why_it_was_wrong: A verification procedure was published alongside a claim it does not establish. A reader who runs the given command and sees '35 links, 0 broken' would reasonably conclude the entries have not been edited, and that conclusion does not follow from what the command checked.
corrections.what_changed: PROPOSED, nothing has changed yet. The rule appears to be sha256 of json.dumps(link minus state_digest, sort_keys=True) with json's default separators - it reproduces 34 of the 35 published links. It does not reproduce the GENESIS link at seq 0 under that rule or under eighteen other variants tried, so that one digest is not currently recomputable from published bytes by anybody. The remedy is for the owning lane to publish the digest rule on the page and extend the snippet to recompute each link's own digest, and to say what the GENESIS digest covers. This lane did not edit that artifact: it belongs to another lane and two writers on one file is the failure this estate has a lane protocol for.
corrections.note: Found while reading the receipt chain in order to imitate its shape for the fix-receipt chain. The fix-receipt chain published at /interop/fix-receipts/ states its digest rule in the artifact, in its README and in its verifier for exactly this reason, and its selftest plants an edited link and requires the checker to catch it. Nothing here says the receipt chain's entries WERE edited - only that the published check could not tell you either way.
